tools.name: list_terminals
tools.description: List terminals attached to this chat, and attached servers that have no session yet (offline_servers). These are the only servers you can reach: nocterm holds their credentials, so never connect on your own with ssh. When the list is empty, tell the user to attach a terminal or server to the chat

tools.name: open_terminal
tools.description: Connect to an attached offline server in the background, without disturbing the user; returns its terminal_id once connected. If it fails, tell the user in one short sentence why and stop

inputSchema.title: OpenTerminal
inputSchema.description: Opens an allowlisted server or reuses its already connected terminal.

server_id.description: A `server_id` from the terminals or offline servers in `list_terminals`.

tools.name: read_terminal
tools.description: Read bounded output of an attached terminal

tools.name: send_input
tools.description: Send text to an attached terminal with user approval

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Type one command into a known empty live shell prompt. Requires shell integration; an output pause never proves completion. Prefer exec_command for a reliable exit status

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Run program with separate args and optional stdin on the attached terminal host over its current connection. Local execution passes args directly; SSH renders a POSIX command line, so arbitrary args require a POSIX-compatible remote command shell and are not guaranteed on Windows SSH. Fresh process: no inherited terminal cwd, environment, aliases or functions. Use an explicit shell for shell syntax. Returns actual exit status or an owned command_id for read_command/cancel_command. Output is bounded and continuously drained

inputSchema.title: ExecCommand
inputSchema.description: A fresh non-interactive program on this terminal's exact host connection.

tools.name: read_command
tools.description: Read a bounded full snapshot of a command owned by this chat. Does not start or cancel a command; optional yield_ms waits briefly

tools.name: cancel_command
tools.description: Cancel a command owned by this chat. SSH sends TERM and closes its channel; remote descendant termination is best effort

tools.name: transfer_files
tools.description: Copy files and folders between the hosts of two attached terminals: this computer (a local terminal) to a server, a server to this computer, or a server to another server. nocterm relays the data over the connections it already holds, so servers need no credentials for each other and you must never use scp, rsync or ssh between them. Every path is absolute (no ~, no .. components). sources are files or folders on the source host; folders copy recursively, and each source is copied into destination under its own name. destination must be an existing folder; it is never created. Existing files are skipped and counted as skipped unless overwrite is true. Symbolic links and special files are skipped. At most 64 sources per call. Two local terminals are refused: use exec_command. Some environments only allow copies within one server. The copy runs in the background: after optional yield_ms (default 1000) it returns the current state and a transfer_id for read_transfer/cancel_transfer. Poll read_transfer until the state is completed, failed or cancelled. Whole files are published atomically; a cancelled or failed file leaves no partial file

inputSchema.title: TransferFiles
inputSchema.description: Copy files and folders between the hosts of two attached terminals.

source_terminal_id.description: terminal_id whose host holds the sources; a local terminal means this computer.

sources.description: Absolute paths of files or folders on the source host; folders copy recursively.

destination_terminal_id.description: terminal_id whose host receives the copies.

destination.description: Absolute path of an existing folder on the destination host.

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist at the destination; by default they are skipped.

tools.name: read_transfer
tools.description: Read a snapshot of a transfer started by this chat: state, file and byte counts and up to 16 failures. Does not start or cancel a transfer; optional yield_ms waits briefly while it is active

tools.name: cancel_transfer
tools.description: Cancel a transfer started by this chat. Files already published stay in place; files being copied are discarded
